connections: Memory as relationship
Reading brings neurodivergent memory works into conversation with Abram’s phenomenology; compare their questions, not their evidence types.
Memory through the senses
Reading’s cultural-memory inquiry can be contrasted with research on odor-evoked autobiographical memory.
Feeling vs measuring attention
Compare perceived restoration during visual encounters to measurable cognitive changes.
Sound as support or burden
Natural soundscapes and noise-related learning challenges invite questions about context and differing listeners.
Reciprocity meets power
Put Indigenous teachings of relational responsibility beside ecofeminist critiques of hierarchy and labor.
Are we asking animals the right questions?
Pair inquiry ethics with an animal-welfare framework that attends to nonhuman participants.
Research and first-person experience
Read participant accounts alongside an individual autobiographical perspective without generalizing either.
Trees and generations
Contrast a forest scientist’s memoir with cultural histories of long-lived trees.
From diary to inquiry
Look at how narrative attention and nature journaling move toward a researchable question.
Bird encounters, different methods
Compare everyday smartphone reports with an experiment involving recorded birdsong.
Human benefit and animal wellbeing
Explore animal-assisted support alongside the need to respect animal needs and limitations.
Home is remembered
Compare literary place-memory with people’s reported psychological benefits of place attachment.
Gardens, care, and responsibility
Explore gendered labor and reciprocity alongside gardening or intergenerational experience.
